purpose: Research-only refresh; this file is not Feed or published Editorial. Projects absent from Feed remain library candidates.

feedProject.name: AI Engineering Hub
feedProject.action: Original Feed ID refreshed in Editorial; existing 4 improvements, 4 spinoffs and 1 religious idea retained.

projects.name: Google Gen AI SDK
projects.overview: Python client for Gemini Developer API and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform/Vertex AI. It is a remote API SDK, not a local model runtime.
projects.requirements: Python >=3.11; install google-genai. Configure a Gemini API key or Google Cloud project/location and authentication for Vertex AI. Optional httpx/aiohttp extras affect transport.
projects.quickStart: Create an isolated Python environment, install google-genai, configure provider credentials only in environment variables, then follow the README sync or async client example. Add timeouts and explicit error handling.
projects.costs: SDK is open source; model/API usage, cloud infrastructure and egress may incur provider charges. Local client code does not make inference local.
projects.localVsCloud: Client code runs locally; inference is remote through Gemini Developer API or Vertex AI. The SDK does not ship a local inference engine.
projects.alternatives: Direct REST calls, Vertex AI client libraries, or other provider SDKs; compare auth and feature coverage before switching.
projects.limitations: Model availability and billing depend on the selected service and project. Credentials must not be committed; tests with mocks do not prove live provider behavior.

improvements.title: Recorded-response contract tests
improvements.problem: Provider changes can break request shape or response parsing without a deterministic local regression test.
improvements.approach: Add sanitized fixtures and mock transport tests for sync, async, tool-call and structured-output responses.
steps: Select representative non-sensitive response shapes.
Store minimal fixtures with SDK version metadata.
Run tests without network access.
Review fixture changes against upstream schema updates.
improvements.metric: Offline contract-test pass rate and provider regressions caught before release.
improvements.risks: Fixtures can drift from live APIs; keep a small opt-in integration suite.

improvements.title: Dated model capability matrix
improvements.problem: Developers may assume every model supports the same input, output and tool capabilities.
improvements.approach: Generate a dated capability table from official model metadata and label unknown fields explicitly.
steps: Read official model metadata.
Normalize supported capabilities and source URLs.
Generate a dated JSON/Markdown snapshot.
Flag missing or unverified fields.
improvements.metric: Share of capabilities with a current official source and capture date.
improvements.risks: Metadata may omit capabilities; do not infer unknown values.

spinoffs.title: Arabic Gemini API starter lab
spinoffs.problem: Learners need a reproducible example for credentials, structured output and usage limits without embedding secrets.
spinoffs.approach: Provide a small local starter with environment-only credentials and an offline mock mode.
steps: Create a pinned Python project.
Load credentials only from environment variables.
Add structured-output and mock-response examples.
Document usage limits and provider billing checks.
spinoffs.metric: Offline tests pass and mock/live modes remain clearly separated.
spinoffs.risks: Live calls may incur charges; default to mock mode and require explicit opt-in.

projects.name: Lasm
projects.overview: Lean-based application framework and CLI that compiles shared code to Node, browser, edge and serverless targets.
projects.requirements: Node.js 24+, Lean 4.35.0 (the CLI can install it), and the target platform's own CLI/emulator where required.
projects.quickStart: Scaffold with npm create @lasm@latest, run npm install and npm run dev, then build for Node or a chosen target. Run platform CLIs separately for deployment.
projects.costs: MIT source and CLI are free. Hosting, serverless invocations, databases and platform services are billed by the chosen provider.
projects.localVsCloud: Local development uses lasm dev and local emulators; deployment targets include Node containers, Workers, Lambda, Azure and Google Cloud Functions.
projects.alternatives: Hono or Express for Node-only apps; native platform SDKs where a single target is simpler.
projects.limitations: Platform targets have different evidence levels and prerequisites. Local emulation does not prove production behavior.

improvements.title: Cross-target contract suite
improvements.problem: The same application can behave differently across Node, Workers and serverless targets despite compiling successfully.
improvements.approach: Run identical API contract tests against each target's local runtime and publish known divergences.
steps: Define a deterministic sample API.
Run it on Node and target emulators.
Compare status, headers, body and errors.
Publish a compatibility matrix.
improvements.metric: Targets passing the same contract suite and documented divergences.
improvements.risks: Emulators differ from production; label each test environment.

improvements.title: Template runtime manifest
improvements.problem: Scaffolded projects may resolve different tool versions on another machine.
improvements.approach: Generate a manifest pinning CLI, Lean, Node and platform tool versions for every template.
steps: Inventory scaffold templates.
Record runtime and CLI requirements.
Add clean-install CI for representative templates.
Document reviewed upgrade steps.
improvements.metric: Templates that build from a clean pinned install.
improvements.risks: Pinned tools need maintenance; automate reviewed update proposals.

spinoffs.title: Lean serverless starter gallery
spinoffs.problem: Developers need a comparable view of one endpoint across several serverless targets.
spinoffs.approach: Create small target-specific templates sharing the same contract tests and setup notes.
spinoffs.stack: Lean, Lasm CLI, Docker, Wrangler, AWS SAM
steps: Define a tiny JSON endpoint.
Generate Node, Workers and Lambda variants.
Document local emulator commands.
Measure cold start and memory only when actually run.
spinoffs.metric: Targets with reproducible local startup and passing contract tests.
spinoffs.risks: Provider limits and pricing change; timestamp measured results.

projects.name: MarkItDown
projects.overview: Python utility converting office and media files to Markdown while preserving useful structure for downstream text analysis and LLM workflows.
projects.requirements: Python 3.10–3.14. Install markitdown with format-specific extras or [all]. Optional Azure services need cloud credentials.
projects.quickStart: Create a virtual environment, install markitdown or a narrow extra such as pdf/docx/pptx, convert a sample file through CLI or Python API, then compare headings, tables and links with the source.
projects.costs: Core local conversion is free. Azure Document Intelligence, Content Understanding and hosted transcription can add usage charges.
projects.localVsCloud: Most formats can be converted locally; optional Azure services provide cloud understanding or transcription.
projects.alternatives: Pandoc, Unstructured and format-specific parsers where fidelity or control matters more than a common Markdown output.
projects.limitations: Conversion is not pixel-perfect rendering. The process can access resources available to the current user; use narrow converters and isolate untrusted inputs.

improvements.title: Structure-preservation regression corpus
improvements.problem: Converter changes can silently drop tables, links or heading hierarchy.
improvements.approach: Create a small licensed corpus with expected Markdown structure and compare normalized output in CI.
steps: Select redistributable sample documents.
Store expected headings, tables and links.
Run converters and compare normalized structure.
Review diffs after parser upgrades.
improvements.risks: A small corpus may not represent every format; document coverage and licensing.

improvements.title: Restricted-input conversion profile
improvements.problem: Untrusted files may trigger broader file or network access than a conversion pipeline expects.
improvements.approach: Add an allowlisted wrapper with file-size limits and a restricted worker directory.
steps: Define accepted extensions and size limits.
Copy inputs into a temporary directory.
Disable network for local-only conversion.
Record output provenance and rejected inputs.
improvements.metric: Unsafe inputs rejected and conversions confined to allowed directories.
improvements.risks: Sandboxing is defense in depth, not a guarantee; platform-specific controls need review.

spinoffs.title: Offline document-to-Markdown workbench
spinoffs.problem: Learners need to inspect local documents without sending them to a hosted conversion service.
spinoffs.approach: Build a local interface showing the original file beside converted Markdown and extracted structure.
spinoffs.stack: Python, MarkItDown, SQLite, local web UI
steps: Add drag-and-drop for selected formats.
Run conversion in a local worker.
Display headings, tables and links.
Export with source filename and converter version.
spinoffs.metric: Local conversion coverage and key-structure preservation.
spinoffs.risks: Malformed documents can consume resources; impose size and time limits.

projects.name: Minecraft Agent Harness
projects.overview: Node harness allowing LLM agents to act in Minecraft Java, persist named sessions and use shell tools; supports multi-agent sessions and Docker/E2B/local execution.
projects.requirements: Node.js 22.19+, Minecraft Java 1.21.6, a model-provider API key; bundled dev server needs Java 21. Docker or E2B isolates shell access; local-folder fallback runs commands as the current user.
projects.quickStart: Install dependencies, start the bundled Paper server with npm run server, then start an agent with a bounded objective. Prefer the documented Docker sandbox and inspect the effective backend before running.
projects.costs: MIT source is free. Model API, E2B, hosted server and cloud compute may incur charges.
projects.localVsCloud: Local Paper server and Docker are supported; E2B is an optional hosted sandbox. The local-folder fallback is not isolated.
projects.alternatives: Mindcraft and other Minecraft agent projects; compare protocol support, sandboxing and session persistence.
projects.limitations: Shell access is powerful. Avoid unsandboxed mode with sensitive files; use disposable worlds and bounded objectives.

improvements.title: Explicit opt-in for unsandboxed local shell
improvements.problem: When Docker and E2B are unavailable, the fallback can run commands as the current user.
improvements.approach: Require a clear opt-in for unsandboxed mode and display the selected backend before startup.
steps: Detect the selected sandbox backend.
Refuse local unsandboxed mode without an explicit flag.
Print a capability and filesystem warning.
Test every backend-selection path.
improvements.metric: Zero accidental unsandboxed starts in the test suite.
improvements.risks: A strict default may affect scripts; provide migration guidance.

improvements.title: Deterministic session replay
improvements.problem: Agent behavior is hard to debug when observations and tool outcomes cannot be replayed.
improvements.approach: Record structured game observations and tool results for replay in a disposable test world.
improvements.stack: Node.js, JSONL, Paper server, deterministic fixtures
steps: Define a versioned event schema.
Record a short non-sensitive session.
Replay against a disposable world.
Compare expected and actual state transitions.
improvements.metric: Replay success rate and action divergence count.
improvements.risks: Game state and model output can be nondeterministic; distinguish environment replay from model replay.

spinoffs.title: Classroom quests in a disposable world
spinoffs.problem: Educators need bounded tasks where students can inspect agent actions without exposing personal files.
spinoffs.approach: Provide scripted objectives, a resettable world and a visible action log.
steps: Create non-destructive objectives.
Start each session in a fresh world and sandbox.
Display tool calls and game outcomes.
Reset the world after each lesson.
spinoffs.metric: Task completion with a complete action log and successful reset.
spinoffs.risks: Agents may act unpredictably; restrict commands and supervise sessions.

projects.name: NVIDIA OpenShell
projects.overview: Runtime and gateway for autonomous agents with policy-controlled filesystem, network and credential access; includes local sandboxing, SDKs and Kubernetes deployment.
projects.requirements: Linux, macOS on Apple Silicon, or Windows with experimental WSL2; Docker, Podman or host virtualization. Kubernetes needs a CNI enforcing NetworkPolicy.
projects.quickStart: Install the CLI with the official installer, start the local gateway, then follow Run Your First Agent. The default sandbox image is minimal Ubuntu and does not include an agent; configure an agent separately.
projects.costs: Apache-2.0 source is free. Model/API use and optional hosted infrastructure or Kubernetes clusters may incur charges.
projects.localVsCloud: Local gateway and sandbox are supported; Kubernetes/Helm and hosted launchables are deployment alternatives. OpenShell is not a model provider.
projects.alternatives: Docker/Podman with custom policies, devcontainers and other agent sandbox runtimes; compare policy enforcement and credential handling.
projects.limitations: OS support varies; Windows WSL2 is experimental in the README. External materials accessed by agents have separate licenses. Telemetry can be disabled using documented settings.

improvements.title: Policy dry-run visualizer
improvements.problem: A policy file can be hard to audit before an agent requests access.
improvements.approach: Simulate filesystem, network and secret access and show allow/deny decisions without executing the agent.
steps: Define representative access requests.
Run policy evaluation in dry-run mode.
Render allowed and denied resources with reasons.
Export a reviewable policy diff.
improvements.metric: Policy-case coverage and unexpected permissions found before a run.
improvements.risks: Simulator must match runtime enforcement; label unsupported policy constructs.

improvements.title: Policy drift regression suite
improvements.problem: Runtime or policy updates may unintentionally widen access.
improvements.approach: Keep versioned least-privilege fixtures and compare effective permissions across releases.
improvements.stack: OpenShell CLI, YAML, pytest, GitHub Actions
steps: Create role-specific policy fixtures.
Capture effective policy decisions.
Run against pinned and candidate versions.
Review unexpected permission changes.
improvements.metric: Unexpected permission changes per release and fixture coverage.
improvements.risks: Policy semantics may change; pin versions and require human review.

spinoffs.title: Local sandbox templates for Python agents
spinoffs.problem: Developers repeatedly configure filesystem and network restrictions for simple agents.
spinoffs.approach: Publish minimal policy templates with a local smoke test and documented trade-offs.
steps: Choose a narrow sample task.
Allow only required folders and hosts.
Run a disposable agent and inspect denied requests.
Document revocation and cleanup.
spinoffs.metric: Time to create a least-privilege sandbox and unnecessary grants per template.
spinoffs.risks: Templates must be adapted to each threat model; do not label them universally safe.

projects.name: Pydantic AI
projects.overview: Typed Python SDK for agent loops, tools, structured outputs, provider abstraction, evaluations, tracing and durable execution integrations.
projects.requirements: Python >=3.11; install pydantic-ai with uv. Live providers need credentials; built-in TestModel supports tests without a live API key.
projects.quickStart: Create a Python project, install pydantic-ai, follow the simple agent example, use TestModel in unit tests, and configure a provider via environment variables only for live calls.
projects.costs: MIT SDK can run locally. Provider inference, optional gateway, observability and durable workflow infrastructure may incur costs.
projects.localVsCloud: Orchestration runs in Python; inference can use hosted providers or local models such as Ollama. Durable execution depends on the selected backend.
projects.alternatives: Direct provider SDKs, LangChain/LangGraph or Haystack depending on orchestration and retrieval requirements.
projects.limitations: Provider behavior varies. Durable execution and tracing need extra infrastructure; TestModel does not prove live provider behavior.

improvements.title: Per-run budget guard
improvements.problem: Agent loops and retries can consume more calls or tokens than expected.
improvements.approach: Check usage before each additional model call and stop or request approval at a hard limit.
steps: Capture usage after each model call.
Define soft and hard run limits.
Stop or request approval before exceeding the hard limit.
Test guard behavior with TestModel and mocked usage.
improvements.metric: Budget overrun rate and percentage of runs with complete usage records.
improvements.risks: Usage units differ by provider; mark unavailable estimates.

improvements.title: Provider fallback contract tests
improvements.problem: A fallback model may return a different structure or tool behavior than the primary model.
improvements.approach: Test the same typed output and tool contract across providers using mocks and opt-in live tests.
steps: Define typed output and tool fixtures.
Test validation and error paths with TestModel.
Add mocked provider-specific cases.
Keep live tests opt-in and versioned.
improvements.metric: Contract pass rate across selected providers and fallback schema failures.
improvements.risks: Mocks may not capture provider quirks; separate live checks from offline tests.

spinoffs.title: Arabic support agent with cited answers
spinoffs.problem: A support workflow needs Arabic answers tied to approved documentation and abstention when evidence is missing.
spinoffs.approach: Build a typed agent that retrieves approved help pages and returns source references.
spinoffs.stack: Python, Pydantic AI, local vector store, pytest
steps: Index a small set of public help documents.
Define typed answer and citation fields.
Require factual claims to map to retrieved passages.
Test missing-evidence and abstention cases.
spinoffs.metric: Citation precision and correct abstention rate on a reviewed question set.
spinoffs.risks: Unsupported text may still appear; require human review for consequential responses.

projects.name: uv
projects.overview: Fast Python package and project manager written in Rust; installs Python versions, resolves and locks dependencies, manages projects, scripts and tools.
projects.requirements: Supported OS/architecture; standalone installer or pip/pipx. uv can install Python; projects use pyproject.toml and uv.lock.
projects.quickStart: Install uv, run uv init, add dependencies with uv add, run commands with uv run and commit uv.lock for reproducible installs.
projects.costs: Open-source local tool with no model/API fee. Network downloads and CI runner resources are the main costs.
projects.localVsCloud: Primarily local CLI and CI tooling; can use caches for offline workflows after dependencies are available. It is not a hosted package service.
projects.alternatives: pip plus venv, Poetry, PDM, pip-tools and pipx.
projects.limitations: Fast resolution does not guarantee application compatibility. Native builds and platform-specific dependencies may still fail.

improvements.title: Lockfile drift impact report
improvements.problem: Large lockfile changes are hard to review and may upgrade transitive packages unrelated to the requested dependency.
improvements.approach: Summarize added, removed and upgraded packages with dependency paths and platform markers.
steps: Parse before and after lockfiles.
Map changed packages to dependency chains.
Highlight major-version and source changes.
Generate a pull-request report.
improvements.metric: Lockfile changes with an explained dependency path.
improvements.risks: Optional dependency groups may complicate graph reconstruction; label unresolved paths.

improvements.title: Offline cache integrity checker
improvements.problem: A project may work online but fail in a restricted environment without cached artifacts.
improvements.approach: Verify that required wheels and source archives exist before an offline sync.
steps: Read lockfile and platform markers.
Check cache for each required artifact.
Report missing wheels or source archives.
Run a controlled offline sync in a disposable environment.
improvements.metric: Offline sync success rate for declared platforms.
improvements.risks: Caches are platform-specific; report target OS and architecture.

spinoffs.title: AI-course Python environment bootstrap
spinoffs.problem: Students lose time configuring inconsistent Python versions and packages across exercises.
spinoffs.approach: Create course templates with uv, pinned lockfiles and one command to run each lesson's checks.
steps: Create a template pyproject per course unit.
Pin Python and dependency versions in uv.lock.
Add one-command setup and lesson tests.
Document reviewed dependency refreshes.
spinoffs.metric: Setup success rate on clean machines and time to first successful lesson.
spinoffs.risks: Old locks become stale; refresh them through reviewed updates.

projects.name: Onlook
projects.license: Apache-2.0 source; some assets have separate terms
projects.overview: Local-first desktop visual editor that runs a developer's app locally and lets users shape the real interface visually. Source builds can connect a user's own Claude Code or Codex account.
projects.requirements: Source build documented for macOS Apple Silicon or Intel, Git, Node.js 24, Bun 1.4.2 and Xcode Command Line Tools. Agent provider account requirements are separate.
projects.quickStart: For source build, install prerequisites, clone, run bun install --frozen-lockfile --cpu='*', bun run build, then bun dev. No Onlook account or cloud keys are needed for the source build.
projects.costs: Source code is Apache-2.0 and free. Model-provider use may require an existing subscription or API plan. No hosted price inferred.
projects.localVsCloud: Local-first desktop app; project code and dev server run on the computer. Agent provider connection is external.
projects.alternatives: Browser devtools and a conventional code editor; design tools may complement but are not identical to editing a running local codebase.
projects.limitations: The source license does not automatically cover every asset. Current source-build guide is macOS-focused; telemetry choice and provider account terms need review.

improvements.title: Review AI patch before apply
improvements.problem: Visual agent edits can touch multiple files and need a clear approval point.
improvements.approach: Show per-file diffs, preview the rendered result and allow selective accept/reject with a restore point.
steps: Capture working-tree state before edits.
Group changes by file and component.
Preview accepted subsets in the running app.
Allow rollback to the captured state.
improvements.metric: Agent edits reviewed before apply and successful rollback rate.
improvements.risks: Snapshots consume disk and may conflict with concurrent edits; detect external changes.

improvements.title: RTL visual regression matrix
improvements.problem: Arabic interfaces can break through direction, font and responsive changes.
improvements.approach: Add screenshot tests for RTL pages across mobile, tablet and desktop.
steps: Create representative Arabic pages.
Capture screenshots at fixed viewports.
Compare direction-sensitive layout regions.
Report diffs for human review.
improvements.metric: RTL regressions detected and false-positive rate.
improvements.risks: Font rendering differs by OS; pin test environment and review diffs.

spinoffs.title: Local design-to-code learning playground
spinoffs.problem: Students need to experiment with layout changes on a real local app while retaining source control.
spinoffs.approach: Create a disposable starter app with visual edits, Git snapshots and guided CSS diff review.
steps: Generate a small RTL/LTR starter app.
Open it in a local workspace.
Make a visual change and inspect the diff.
Reset or keep the change with a short explanation.
spinoffs.metric: Exercises completed with a reviewed reproducible diff.
spinoffs.risks: Use disposable sample projects by default, not personal repositories.

projects.name: FailTrace
projects.overview: Early-stage Go CLI that starts from a failed GitHub Actions run, extracts the failing job/step and prepares a local reproduction plan, with Docker reproduction for supported Linux run steps.
projects.requirements: Go 1.24 to build from source; GitHub token is required even for public repositories to access Actions logs. Docker is needed for containerized reproduction; private repos need Actions-read permission.
projects.quickStart: Install a release binary or go install the module, authenticate with GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN or GitHub CLI, inspect a failed Actions run, then follow the plan/repro commands. Review limitations before treating local output as equivalent to CI.
projects.costs: MIT CLI is free. GitHub API usage is subject to account/API limits; Docker uses local resources. Hosted CI costs remain with the repository owner.
projects.localVsCloud: Analysis runs locally after downloading logs and workflow metadata; GitHub API access is remote. Reproduction runs locally in Docker for supported Linux steps.
projects.alternatives: nektos/act runs workflows locally from workflow files; FailTrace starts from a failed run and extracts context, so the tools are complementary.
projects.limitations: README labels the project early development. Reproduction covers Linux jobs with run scripts; service containers, secrets, reusable workflows and macOS/Windows runners may be partial or unsupported.

improvements.title: Secret redaction before diagnostic export
improvements.problem: CI logs may contain credentials or private values that should not be copied into tickets or LLM tools.
improvements.approach: Redact known patterns before writing JSON/Markdown and keep raw logs out of reports.
improvements.stack: Go, regexp, structured log parser, tests
steps: Identify sensitive token patterns.
Redact before serialization.
Add synthetic-secret fixtures.
Document best-effort limits and manual review.
improvements.metric: Zero synthetic test secrets in exported reports.
improvements.risks: Pattern redaction can miss unknown secrets; never treat it as a guarantee.

improvements.title: CI/local environment drift report
improvements.problem: A local reproduction may fail because the local OS or toolchain differs from the original runner.
improvements.approach: Compare workflow-declared tools and runner image with the local reproduction plan.
improvements.stack: Go, workflow YAML parser, Docker inspect
steps: Extract OS and toolchain requirements.
Capture local image and installed tool versions.
Generate exact/approximate/unknown matches.
Mark partial reproductions clearly.
improvements.metric: Reproduction plans with an explicit environment-drift report.
improvements.risks: Dynamic workflow expressions may be unresolved; label them unknown.

spinoffs.title: CI failure runbook generator
spinoffs.problem: Teams repeatedly diagnose similar failures without a consistent record of cause and verified fix.
spinoffs.approach: Generate a local Markdown runbook with redacted context, reproduction status and original-run links.
steps: Fetch run metadata and selected failure context.
Redact sensitive values.
Generate a checklist and reproduction status.
Let a maintainer mark a resolution verified.
spinoffs.metric: Time to create a reviewed runbook and share of entries with verified resolutions.
spinoffs.risks: Never label a suspected cause confirmed without maintainer review.

presentationRequirements: For projects present in Feed, use the original Feed ID and show overview, requirements, quickStart, costs, local/cloud mode, alternatives and limitations.
Projects absent from Feed remain in the internal research library and must not appear as published site cards.
Display metrics capture time, license, archived state and last push; cumulative Stars are not daily growth.
Preserve proposal order and stable idea links; label difficulty as an estimate and keep testStatus=not_run unless testEvidence exists.
